baseline.first_run: This is the first report for this scope. Day-over-day changes (closed, new, dismissed) start with the next report.
baseline.label: Baseline.
baseline.other: No comparable previous report was found, so no day-over-day changes are shown.
baseline.owner_set_changed: The set of owners changed since the previous report, so this report starts a new baseline and shows no day-over-day changes.
baseline.previous_unreadable: The previous report's snapshot.json could not be read (truncated or corrupt), so this report starts a new baseline and shows no changes since the previous report.
baseline.short.first_run: baseline, first report for this scope
baseline.short.previous_unreadable: baseline, the previous snapshot was unreadable
campaigns.angular: Framework major upgrade: plan as a migration, not a routine bump
campaigns.empty: No single fix currently closes alerts in two or more repositories.
campaigns.empty_repo: No package currently has two or more open alerts in this repository.
campaigns.lead: Each row is one fix (a package upgrade) that closes open Dependabot alerts in several repositories at once. Larger campaigns close more alerts per change.
campaigns.lead_repo: Each row is one upgrade of a package that closes several open Dependabot alerts in this repository at once (all its advisories). Larger rows close more alerts per change.
campaigns.shrunk: No longer spanning several repositories, alerts still open:
campaigns.shrunk_repo: No longer grouping several alerts, alerts still open:
campaigns.unconfirmed: Not completed, remaining alerts hidden by lost coverage (unknown, not fixed):
changes.baseline: Not available in a baseline report.
changes.none: No alerts were opened or closed since the previous report.
changes.outcome_resolved: No longer open (fixed or resolved on GitHub)
changes.reached_zero: Repositories that reached zero open alerts (all scanners readable):
changes.reached_zero_partial: 0 open in covered scanners (partial coverage, not counted as zero):
changes.title: Changes since the previous report
coverage.full_count: Repositories with all three scanners readable: {n}.
coverage.lead: Repositories with at least one scanner whose alerts could be read: {scanned} of {total}. Repositories without coverage are not counted in any total: zero alerts there does not mean zero risk.
coverage.legend.no_permission: The account that ran the report cannot read these alerts. It needs security-alert read access to the repository, or an owner or security manager role. Open alerts may exist that this report does not show.
coverage.legend.not_enabled: The scanner is turned off for this repository. On a private repository this can also mean that the paid GitHub security product (Code Security or Secret Protection) is not turned on for it. Action: enable it (this requires available license seats). No alerts are counted for it.
coverage.legend.not_licensed: GitHub reports that the organization has no license for this feature. Action: obtain licenses (GitHub Code Security or Secret Protection) before it can be enabled. No alerts are counted for it.
coverage.legend.ok: The scanner is enabled and its alerts were read. Zero alerts here means zero open alerts.
coverage.legend.unavailable: The status could not be determined: the endpoint did not answer (an older GitHub Enterprise Server, a temporary error), or, on the organization endpoints, the account is not an org owner and GitHub answered 404 to the Dependabot status check (security managers can get that). The status is unknown and no alerts are counted for it.
coverage.lost_baseline: Not available in a baseline report.
coverage.lost_lead: Alerts open in the previous report that are no longer visible because the scanner coverage of their repository was lost: {n}. They are not counted as closed.
coverage.lost_none: No alerts left the view because of lost coverage.
coverage.no_gaps: Every scanner is readable on every repository in scope.
dismissals.baseline: Not available in a baseline report. The full record of dismissed alerts is listed below.
dismissals.none_period: No alerts were dismissed since the previous report.
dismissals.none_record: No dismissed or resolved-as-exception alerts are on record.
footer.text: Generated by github-security-remediation from snapshot.json ({generated}). Self-contained: no scripts and no external resources. Links point to {host}. Secret values are never fetched or shown.
kpi.baseline_no_delta: Baseline: no previous report to compare
kpi.p1_sub: highest band, score of {min} or more
kpi.zero_partial: 0 open in covered scanners (partial coverage, not counted): {n}
kpi.zero_sub: reached zero since the previous report: {n}
method.activity.within_180_days: Repository pushed within the last 180 days
method.activity.within_30_days: Repository pushed within the last 30 days
method.epss: EPSS percentile of {threshold} or more (highest matching tier only)
method.g_severity: Base points by severity (Dependabot and code scanning)
method.lead: All weights below are read from the snapshot this report was built from ({generated}), so the report shows exactly what was applied. They stay stable across runs.
method.priority_intro: Each open alert gets a score from the signals below. The sum is clamped to the range {lo} to {hi}.
method.rule.baseline: When there is no previous report, the set of owners changed, or the previous snapshot cannot be read, the report is a baseline and shows no day-over-day changes.
method.rule.coverage: Only scanners with coverage OK are counted. A repository is at zero, or reaches zero, only when all three scanners are readable; 0 open alerts with a scanner missing is listed as partial coverage. A repository without coverage is never reported as zero alerts.
method.rule.delta: Day delta = open alerts now minus open alerts in the previous report of the same scope.
method.rule.determinism: Every number comes from snapshot.json and diff.json. Rendering the same inputs again produces the same report.
method.rule.lost: An alert that disappears because its scanner coverage was lost is listed under lost coverage, not as closed.
method.rule.secrets: Secret values are never fetched or stored (hide_secret=true). Only the secret type and its validity are shown.
method.secret.base: Base points for any exposed secret
method.text.clusters: open Dependabot alerts grouped by ecosystem:package:advisory (and angular:<major>), kept when they span >= 2 repos; in a single-repo report, grouped by ecosystem:package (and angular:<major>), kept when they hold >= 2 alerts
method.text.ranking: per repo with coverage, sorted by (-max_priority, -p1_count, -open, repo)

report.title: GitHub security remediation report
strategy.partial_view: Partial view: only repositories and alerts visible to the account that ran the report

strategy.repo_filter_view: Only the repositories named for this report
summary.changes: Since the previous report: {closed} closed ({dismissed} dismissed), {new} new
summary.coverage: Coverage: {scanned} of {total} scanned; {none} without any readable scanner (not counted as zero)
summary.full_report: Full report with details per repository, waves and methodology: report.html
summary.narrative_note: Every number quoted in these notes comes from the snapshot and the diff of this report.
summary.open: Open alerts: {open} ({delta} vs. previous report; hidden by lost coverage, not fixed: {lost})
summary.partial: Partial view for {owners}: only repositories and alerts visible to the account that ran the report
table.more: Showing {shown} of {total}. The full list is in snapshot.json.
top.empty: No open alerts in repositories with coverage.
top.lead: Repositories with open alerts, ranked by their highest alert priority, then P1 count, then open alerts (showing {n} of {total}). Only repositories with readable coverage are ranked.
trend.desc: From {start} to {end}, open alerts went from {first} to {last}.
trend.single: The trend line appears once there are two or more reports for this scope (each run counts, even on the same day).
wave.1.desc: Every open exposed secret and every P1 alert. Rotate secrets first: closing the alert does not revoke the credential.
wave.1.title: Wave 1: now
wave.2.desc: P2 alerts, plus alerts covered by a campaign that spans five or more repositories.
wave.2.title: Wave 2: next
wave.3.desc: Everything else, to schedule with regular maintenance.
wave.3.title: Wave 3: planned
waves.empty: No open alerts in this wave.
waves.lead: Open alerts split into three waves so the team works on the most urgent items first. Within a wave, alerts are ordered by priority score.
